audit_findings.title: Post-year-end acquisition breaks claim coherence
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; June 2026 debt was $195.024m above December 2025 and first-half 2026 acquisition cash outflow was $400.816m
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE numerator excludes subsequent and partial-year acquisition economics, while current shares, cash and financing enter the equity bridge; omitted acquired OE raises value, while omitted interest and maintenance capital lower it.
audit_findings.evidence: In January 2026, we expanded our geographic footprint when we acquired the assets of RGL, Inc. (dba Mountain State Waste), which consists of collection operations in West Virginia and a transfer station operation in southwestern Pennsylvania (the “Mountain State Waste Acquisition”).
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, not merely a possible future risk. The direction and net OE adjustment remain unresolved because the filings do not isolate acquired operating cash generation and maintenance requirements. The financing scale is more than three times the $60.2m anchor, so the mismatch is reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Build current-perimeter OE using filed acquisition dates and pro forma results, annualize acquired operating earnings, interest and maintenance capital, include full-year contributions from the 2025 acquisitions, and reconcile the $93.086m restricted acquisition cash so it is not added after being spent.

audit_findings.title: Landfill closure cash obligations may escape owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.045m of 2025 obligations settled, equal to 11.7% of the $60.2m anchor; $192.722m accrued and $412.278m undiscounted future payments
audit_findings.mechanism: OE adds back landfill-related depreciation and amortization, but liability settlements can bypass both reported property additions and current-period earnings; any omitted normalized settlement cash directly overstates OE and every discounted forecast year.
audit_findings.evidence: We have material financial obligations relating to final capping, closure and post-closure costs of our existing owned or operated landfills and will have material financial obligations with respect to any disposal facilities that we may own or operate in the future.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash obligations and their scale are demonstrated, while their omission from the OE calculation is not yet proven. The 2025 settlements alone equal 11.7% of anchor OE, and the much larger filed payment schedule makes this reasonably capable of changing the valuation materially. Accretion expense captures financing through time, not the underlying settlement cash.
audit_findings.action: Trace each 2025 and first-half 2026 capping, closure, post-closure and remediation payment through OE and maintenance capital; deduct a normalized recurring amount exactly once and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Known landfill runoff is absent from the perimeter ruling
audit_findings.mechanism: NCES and Ontario County earnings remain in anchor OE and consolidated growth, while their expected 2027 and 2028 shutdowns can reduce OE, raise third-party disposal and transport costs, require capping cash and invalidate terminal continuation unless replacement economics are modeled.
audit_findings.evidence: Given our current expected run rate and remaining available capacity at our NCES Landfill in Bethlehem, New Hampshire, we may consume all remaining permitted capacity at our NCES Landfill during the fiscal year ending December 31, 2027 (“fiscal year 2027”).
audit_findings.explanation: The closure timing and absence of an explicit runoff adjustment are demonstrated. However, the filings supplied do not isolate either landfill's OE, actual throughput, replacement margins or closure cash, so the record cannot establish the valuation magnitude. Replacement capacity and pricing could offset some effects, but no such offset is presently quantified.
audit_findings.action: Obtain facility-level revenue, margin, maintenance capital and closure-payment schedules; model lost internalization, third-party disposal and transport costs, and probability-weighted replacement capacity, then rerun explicit-period and terminal values.

audit_findings.title: Financed asset additions may be missing from maintenance capital
audit_findings.magnitude: gross exposure of $45.311m in 2025, equal to 75.3% of the $60.2m anchor, before separating maintenance from growth and avoiding double counting
audit_findings.mechanism: If OE deducts only $245.071m of cash property additions while adding back depreciation on finance-leased operating assets, required maintenance investment acquired through non-cash financing is omitted from OE.
audit_findings.evidence: We lease vehicles, equipment, property and other non-core equipment in the ordinary course of our business.
audit_findings.explanation: The $45.311m of finance-lease asset additions is filed, but the record does not prove that the OE calculation omitted it or establish what portion was maintenance. Nevertheless, the gross pool is three-quarters of anchor OE, making the possible error reasonably capable of materially changing value even if only part qualifies.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the OE maintenance-capital schedule to cash additions, finance-lease additions and other financed assets asset by asset; classify maintenance versus growth and confirm lease principal is not deducted a second time before rerunning the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Current interest cost benefits from expiring hedges
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.7m annual interest change per 100 basis points on June 2026 variable-rate exposure, equal to 7.8% of the $60.2m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this equity-level OE retains interest and debt is not deducted in the bridge, higher post-hedge or refinancing rates reduce forecast OE directly.
audit_findings.evidence: These agreements mature or have matured between February 2026 and June 2028.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a forward-looking exposure rather than a demonstrated valuation error. The June 2026 filing reports $515.0m of swaps extending from December 2026 through February 2030 and approximately $470.0m of variable-rate debt exposure, so the earlier expiry schedule has evolved but repricing risk remains. The filed sensitivity shows potentially meaningful OE exposure.
audit_findings.action: Maintain a maturity-level debt and swap schedule, update it each filing, forecast interest using contractual margins and post-expiry rates, and rerun scenarios if the normalized annual burden differs materially from the interest embedded in FY2025 OE.
